question: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad mean?
answer: “Elimination/rejection of discord, mischief or strife.”
facts: • Radd means rejection/repelling; fasaad refers to disorder or corruption. • Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017.

question: What is the currency of New Zealand?
answer: New Zealand dollar (NZD).
facts: • Its symbol is commonly written as NZ$. • Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.

question: What is Pakistan’s longest river?
answer: The Indus River.
facts: • The Indus River system is vital for Pakistan’s irrigation and agriculture. • Major tributaries include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej and Kabul.

question: What is condensation?
answer: The change of water vapour/gas into liquid.
facts: • Cloud formation involves condensation of water vapour. • Cooling air can cause water vapour to condense.

question: Which languages/technologies are used to build websites?
answer: HTML, CSS and JavaScript are core web technologies; PHP and Java may be used on the server side.
facts: • HTML structures content; CSS styles it; JavaScript adds interactivity. • Java and JavaScript are different languages.

question: What does NATO stand for, and when was it established?
answer: North Atlantic Treaty Organization; established 4 April 1949.
facts: • The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington, D.C. • NATO’s founding membership comprised 12 countries.

question: What percentage of Pakistan is covered by forests?
answer: A single figure depends on the definition and dataset; the often-quoted 2.2% is an older estimate and should not be treated as a current definitive statistic.
facts: • Forest cover statistics vary by whether plantations, natural forest and tree cover are included. • Use the latest Pakistan Economic Survey or FAO dataset for a dated figure.

question: Complete: “He will ___ here by now.”
answer: have reached — “He will have reached here by now” is grammatically possible but more natural is “He will have arrived here by now.”
facts: • Future perfect: will have + past participle. • “Arrive” is usually intransitive; say “arrive here,” not “reach here” in formal usage.

question: Which area is called Babul Islam?
answer: Sindh.
facts: • The title means “Gateway of Islam” in common South Asian historical usage. • Muhammad bin Qasim’s campaign in Sindh took place in 711–712 CE.

question: How many major rivers are commonly listed for Balochistan?
answer: Some general-knowledge sources list seven major rivers, but the count depends on how rivers and seasonal streams are classified.
facts: • Important rivers/streams include Hingol, Dasht, Porali, Hub, Zhob, Nari and Bolan. • Much of Balochistan is arid, and many waterways are seasonal.

question: What is the inverse of a scalar matrix?
answer: The inverse of a non-zero scalar matrix is also a scalar matrix.
facts: • If A = aI and a ≠ 0, then A⁻¹ = (1/a)I. • A zero scalar matrix has no inverse because its determinant is zero.

question: What is the last letter when “UTYEAB” is arranged alphabetically?
answer: Y.
facts: • Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y. • The final letter after sorting is Y.

question: Which is Pakistan's largest district by area?
answer: Chagai District, Balochistan, is commonly listed as the largest by area.
facts: • Chagai lies in western Balochistan near the borders with Iran and Afghanistan. • District boundaries or rankings can change after administrative reorganizations.

question: What is an empty set?
answer: A set with no elements; it is a finite set with cardinality zero.
facts: • It is represented by ∅ or {}. • The empty set is a subset of every set.

question: Who is known by the title “Kaleemullah”?
answer: Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him.
facts: • The title refers to his speaking with Allah, as described in Islamic tradition. • Other traditional titles include Khalilullah for Prophet Ibrahim and Ruhullah for Prophet Isa.

question: Who was President when Pakistan's 1956 Constitution came into force?
answer: Iskander Mirza.
facts: • Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956. • The 1956 Constitution established a parliamentary system and was abrogated in 1958.

question: Who partitioned Bengal in 1905?
answer: Lord Curzon; the partition took effect in 1905, not 1913.
facts: • The partition was annulled in 1911. • The 1905 partition helped stimulate the Swadeshi Movement.

question: When did Abu Bakr (RA) lead the Hajj, and when was Hajj made obligatory?
answer: Abu Bakr (RA) led the pilgrimage in 9 AH; many Islamic histories place the obligation of Hajj in 9 AH as well.
facts: • Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) performed his Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH. • Some references distinguish the date Hajj became obligatory from the first pilgrimage led by Abu Bakr.

question: When was the Badshahi Mosque built?
answer: It was commissioned by Aurangzeb and completed in 1673.
facts: • It is located in Lahore, opposite Lahore Fort. • It was one of the world's largest mosques at the time of its construction.

question: Which country voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in 1947?
answer: Afghanistan cast the sole vote against Pakistan's admission in the UN General Assembly vote.
facts: • Pakistan was admitted on 30 September 1947. • The General Assembly vote was 53 in favour, one against, with abstentions recorded in the historical table.

question: What was the approximate Muslim force at the Battle of Badr?
answer: About 313 Muslims, according to the traditional Islamic account.
facts: • The battle took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • The Muslim force was much smaller than the Quraysh force in traditional accounts.

question: In which Hijri year was zakat made obligatory?
answer: Commonly dated to 2 AH for formal obligatory zakat.
facts: • Zakat is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. • Its rate and eligibility depend on the type of wealth and the relevant conditions.

question: When is friction between a tyre and the road at its maximum useful level?
answer: Near the limit of static friction, just before the tyre begins to skid; “hard braking” alone is not a precise scientific answer.
facts: • Locked, sliding tyres usually have less friction than tyres rolling near the peak grip threshold. • Anti-lock braking systems help prevent wheel lockup and maintain steering control.

question: Which Microsoft Word feature creates decorative text?
answer: WordArt.
facts: • WordArt applies stylized effects to text. • It is useful for titles and decorative headings, not usually long body text.

question: Which battle is called Jang-e-Furqan?
answer: The Battle of Badr.
facts: • It took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • The word Furqan means a criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

question: How many Muslims were initially present at the Battle of Uhud?
answer: About 1,000 initially; around 300 withdrew before the battle, leaving about 700.
facts: • The Battle of Uhud took place in 3 AH (625 CE). • The Muslims faced a larger Meccan force.

question: Who enslaved Hazrat Bilal (RA) before his freedom?
answer: Umayyah ibn Khalaf.
facts: • Bilal (RA) was persecuted in Makkah for accepting Islam. • Abu Bakr (RA) purchased and freed him according to traditional Islamic accounts.

question: What is the McMahon Line?
answer: A line drawn in the eastern sector of the disputed China-India boundary under the 1914 Simla Convention; it is not the name of the entire China-India border.
facts: • India accepts the line as its boundary in the eastern sector; China disputes it. • The line was named after British diplomat Henry McMahon.

question: What is the world's largest island?
answer: Greenland.
facts: • Australia is classified as a continent, not an island in the usual school-geography convention. • Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

question: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
answer: Prophet Dawud (David), peace be upon him.
facts: • Zabur is commonly identified with the Psalms in comparative religious studies. • Dawud is also known as a king and prophet in Islamic tradition.

question: In which year did Shah Waliullah die?
facts: • He was a major Islamic scholar and reformer in South Asia. • He translated the Quran into Persian; his son Shah Abdul Qadir later produced a major Urdu translation.
